Please remember that most RCTs have a parallel design. In RCTs with parallel group design, each group of participants is exposed to only
one of the study interventions. This is useful for comparing both bene�cial and adverse e�ects of either an active drug against placebo (Q2)
or two or more active drugs. An RCT has a cross-over design when each of the participants is given all the study interventions in successive
periods, with the order being determined at random. Crossover trials produce within participant comparisons, whereas parallel designs
produce between participant comparisons. As each participant is also a control in crossover trials, valid results can be obtained with fewer
participants than would be required with a parallel design. Hence, this design is likely to be the most suited for Q1. When two or more
experimental interventions are not only compared separately but also in combination and against a control in an RCT, then it is called a
factorial RCT. For Q3 where 'values' are measured, a qualitative design is appropriate.

questions.explanation:
In 1946, Joseph Berkson highlighted that the relative frequency of disease in a group of patients who are hospitalised is inherently biased
when compared to the population served by the hospital (Berkson Bias). This phenomenon is attributable to the way in which the
probabilities of hospitalisation combine in patients with more than one disease (if you have two diseases, your probability of being
hospitalised is greater than the probability associated with either disease separately). If, for example, obese people who have hypertension
have a higher probability of being hospitalised than people with hypertension alone, a spurious association between obesity and anti-
hypertensive drugs can be found. People with self-harm or violence are likely to be over-represented in the psychiatric wards, and this over-
representation will a�ect the aim of the study described in Q1.

questions.emi_instruction: For each of the following scenarios choose the correct option from the responses below
questions.question_text:
You want to develop a single index that re�ects
people's willingness to have socially close contact with immigrants
questions.explanation:
Scales such as CGI consist of items that are based on Likert approach, with a verbal description attached to each point of the scale. These
are useful in the objective measurement of change in the symptom status after an intervention.
A Guttmann Scalogram is a scale composed of several yes/no items in a manner such that if a respondent agrees to the one statement,
he/she is likely to agree to the lower order statements as well. So the total score of the scale represents a single index for the continuum
that is measured. In other words, a person's entire set of responses to all items can be reconstructed from their score. This procedure is also
called cumulative scaling. The Guttman scale is most suitable for hierarchical constructs e.g. social attitudes, political views, developmental
stages, etc. E.g. Bogardus Social Distance Scale is a cumulative scale used to measure the willingness of people in accepting an immigrant
into their social groups (E.g., family, work etc).
Visual analogue scales or pictorial thermometres are often used to assess self-report measures for pain, depression and other mental states
in adults and children. These scales follow a Likert-type pattern but use either numerical or intensity coding for grading a continuum. For
children below the age of 6, and adults with learning disabilities, number/word free versions with smiley faces can be used to generate self-
report measures.
